declared_basis.declared: Chief, 2026-09-10, before the device A1/A2 runs; every threshold is a refusal condition, none admits by default
declared_basis.k: 10, the laptop A1's k (SAE-J-BRIDGE-2026-09-09), so overlaps compare with that record
declared_basis.chunk: 256 features per score chunk, the laptop A1's chunk; memory only, no effect on values
declared_basis.control_layer: a strong control from the laptop control curve (overlap@10 with the hooked layer: 0.047 at layer 2 for the 4B); for the 12B the analogous early layer 3; that curve was measured with the hosted bf16 lens and is the declared basis, not a prediction for the float32 device lens
declared_basis.maximum_control_overlap: 0.5: the laptop curve shows a neighbouring layer shares 0.7-0.8 of top-10 sets, so a control sharing half or more is not a control; 0.5 sits below the neighbour band and far above the strong-control values
declared_basis.check_features: the laptop A1's eight named features, indices carried over unchanged to the 12B dictionary as arbitrary indices; the two-products check is a numerical identity, not a semantic choice
declared_basis.two_product_tolerance: 1e-3 absolute on scores of order 1-40 (laptop top-10 scores 0.26-37.8): float32 chunked accumulation differs at ~1e-5, an orientation error at order 1
declared_basis.convention_threshold: 0.5, the second amendment's table (laptop: raw arm 0.245, gain arm 0.995)
declared_basis.error_budget: raw_reconstruction_threshold 0.5 and lens_score_error_threshold 0.5: a decomposition that leaves half the residual, or half the score, unexplained is not read as a description of the site; denominator_floor 1e-6 against float32 zeros; near-zero refuses. These are refusal lines for out-of-domain agent transcripts whose reconstruction error no one has measured; the run reports the shares whatever they are
declared_basis.a2.identity_tolerance: 1e-3 relative on the emitted token's score: the identity L h = L b + sum z_i L d_i + L e holds to float32 rounding (~1e-6) when the orientation is right and fails at order 1 when it is wrong
declared_basis.layer: dictionary layer_23 = repository layer 24, the first layer the positions file's domain-of-validity statement covers at the action position (W-5 agreement 0.99 from layer 24); the control layer 2 is unchanged

position_weighting.target_reduction: sum over selected target positions, not normalised

manifest.sample_rule: per family, sorted (task_id, step), prompts <= 1500 tokens, every k-th to 25

domain_of_validity.statement: The 4B lens was fitted on 201 prose prompts of 128 tokens, positions 16 to 126, float32 at dimension batch 32; every cell here lies outside that domain (positions 400 to 4,300 in contexts up to 4,300 tokens, agent transcripts, not prose). What is measured of the extrapolation, in the workspace record (WORKSPACE-EXPERIMENTS-2026-09-10, W-5): the six-tool readout through the lens at the action position agrees with the model's own argmax where it resolves, by prompt-length band (<= 1,024 / <= 2,048 / > 2,048 tokens), at 0.99 / 0.99 / 0.98 from layer 24 and 0.92 to 1.00 through layer 33, with no band dependence from layer 24; below layer 24 the readout is unresolved at the 0.001 floor in every band, so no agreement is measured there. That measurement licenses the lens as a readout of the six tool logits at the action position from layer 24 on these contexts, and nothing else: a residual-space A2 reading at any layer below 24, and any reading at the note position, is outside measured validity and is reported as such; a dictionary-direction reading (A1) crosses no capture path. The cross-path term between the fit's width and the capture's width is the registered pairing beside each cell, not part of this statement.

lens.convention: maps[L] is the archive's J{L-1}; L x for a row is x @ J.T

bridge.residual_convention: the dictionary hook is the output of decoder block N; the capture convention numbers that residual as layer N + 1 and the lens keys it as J{N}; the bridge reads layer 24
bridge.score_map: L x = W ((J x) * (1 + w)); the RMS normaliser is a positive per-vector scalar and is dropped so the map is linear; ranks and overlaps are unaffected, score values are not logits
bridge.tensor_reader: safetensors header and bytes, bfloat16 widened to float32 by bit shift

interpretation_limits: A large feature contribution to a lens score is a contribution to that score, at that layer, under that averaging convention. It is not a token probability, not a causal derivative, and not evidence of a workspace, a maintained state, or flexible access.
A description we generate is not a published label and no artifact may present it as one.
